Settings for the MCMC sampler

Source: R/control.R
mcmc_control.Rd

Each iteration makes ess_sweeps updates of the latent values of the observed cells (elliptical slice sampling) and theta_moves pairs of Metropolis moves on the hyperparameters. During burn-in, the proposals adapt and the Gaussian approximation that steers the latent updates is refitted to the chain (twice, at half and three-quarters of burn-in); both are fixed afterwards, so the draws after burn-in come from an exact MCMC. Chains start from dispersed hyperparameters and latent values, so that R-hat in diagnose() can reveal chains that have not mixed.

Usage

mcmc_control(
  n_iter = 3000,
  n_burn = 1000,
  n_store = 250,
  n_chains = 4,
  ess_sweeps = 10,
  theta_moves = 2,
  theta_thin = 1,
  seed = 1,
  n_cores = NULL,
  blas_threads = 1,
  checkpoint_every = 500,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

n_iter

Iterations per chain, burn-in included.

n_burn

Burn-in iterations (adaptation; discarded).

n_store

Posterior draws kept per chain, spread evenly over the iterations after burn-in (the last iteration is always kept). These are the draws used for prediction.

n_chains

Number of chains.

ess_sweeps

Latent updates per iteration.

theta_moves

Hyperparameter move pairs per iteration.

theta_thin

Keep every theta_thin-th iteration of the hyperparameter trace (burn-in included). At least 4 traced iterations must fall after burn-in.

seed

Random seed, any whole number >= 0. Each chain gets its own seed, drawn from this one, and R's default generator is used whatever the session's RNGkind(). The caller's random-number stream is left untouched.

n_cores

Number of worker processes; chains run one per worker. Default: one per chain, at most the number of cores less one. Use 1 to run the chains one after another in this R session.

blas_threads

BLAS threads per worker. One is safest; with an optimised BLAS (MKL, OpenBLAS, Accelerate) and large fits, more may be faster, as long as n_cores * blas_threads does not exceed the cores.

checkpoint_every

Iterations between checkpoints, when fit_areal() is given a checkpoint_dir.

verbose

Print progress: a line per chain after 10 iterations, then every tenth of the run (at most every 500 iterations), with the time left.

Value

A list of the settings.

Details

The defaults are a pilot run. A run for publication is typically much longer (e.g. 40,000 iterations with 8,000 burn-in and theta_thin = 10). Use diagnose() to judge whether a run is long enough.

fit_areal() also accepts a plain list of any of these arguments, e.g. control = list(n_iter = 500); the others take their defaults.

Examples

mcmc_control(n_iter = 500, n_burn = 200, n_store = 100, n_chains = 2)
#> $n_iter
#> [1] 500
#> 
#> $n_burn
#> [1] 200
#> 
#> $n_store
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $n_chains
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $ess_sweeps
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $theta_moves
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $theta_thin
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_cores
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $blas_threads
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $checkpoint_every
#> [1] 500
#> 
#> $verbose
#> [1] TRUE
